summary_en: This work uses the native optical absorption of consumer-grade microplastics to generate photoacoustic contrast in living mammalian tissue without exogenous labels. It distinguishes particles from endogenous signals, resolves microscale features, and tracks microplastics for up to two months in a mouse model, enabling serial studies of biodistribution and clearance.

summary_en: The paper labels premanufactured biomedical polymers with a hydrophobic dye and uses photoacoustic imaging to visualize microscale degradation, including fiber thinning and fragmentation. In a clinically relevant demonstration, the method detects a resorbable P4HB hernia mesh through 15 mm of ex vivo porcine tissue.
